year.shelter: Basks on sunny rocks, stumps and logs, and hides under them; hibernates in holes in the ground and under roots.
year.young: Gives birth to 3–10 live young in July–August (very few lizards do): that's why it's called viviparous, 'live-bearing'.
year.notes: The only lizard found all over Finland, even north of the Arctic Circle. It can drop its tail to escape, and grows a new one. Basking in the morning sun would be great to show.

text.title: Common lizard
text.stalk_hint: A lizard! Get close quietly, then tap Pounce before it darts into hiding.
text.about_looks: A slim brown lizard with a dark stripe down its back and a long tail. Its belly is pale yellow or orange.
text.about_home: Basks on sunny rocks and logs in forests and on bogs, and hides underneath them.
text.about_winter: Sleeps through winter in a hole in the ground or under tree roots.
text.about_young: Unlike most lizards, it doesn't lay eggs: the young are born alive in late summer.
text.about_fact: If something catches its tail, the lizard can drop it and run. It grows a new one.
